transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, we're reviewing the student oral-history project for the spring term before I give final approval. The draft currently proposes participation by grades 7 and 8, one supervising adult per session, cloud-based audio storage, a 90-day retention period, and a public exhibit of selected recordings. I'd like to hear from each of you on the aspects most relevant to your roles before I make my decision. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share some important findings from my classroom pilot. My end-of-pilot notes show that the project is instructionally ready only for grade 8 — not grade 7. Also, each interview session requires exactly two supervising adults, not one, because students are working with recording equipment and community guests simultaneously. The draft plan still has the original scope of grades 7 and 8 and only one adult per session, but my pilot data indicates both of those need to be updated.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical privacy issue. I completed the district privacy review, and it requires three things that differ from the current draft: first, recordings must remain on the district's encrypted internal server — not cloud-based storage; second, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the exhibit closes, not the 90-day retention period currently proposed; and third, signed guardian consent must be obtained before any student records an interview. The draft still uses the preliminary cloud-storage language, so these requirements need to be incorporated before Dr. Chen signs off.
